speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the nature of your cough, and do you have any fever or chest pain? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Chest X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC 9,000 /μL, Hemoglobin 14.0 g/dL, Platelets 230,000 /μL; Chest X-Ray: Bilateral interstitial infiltrates suggestive of pulmonary fibrosis. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax observed.

speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and do you notice them worsening with exertion? REQUEST TEST: Pulmonary Function Tests.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pulmonary Function Tests: Reduced FVC and FEV1 with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio, indicating a restrictive pattern.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of smoking, exposure to asbestos or other lung irritants, or any autoimmune conditions like rheumatoid arthritis? REQUEST TEST: Autoimmune Panel (ANA, RF, CCP).

speaker: Doctor
text: That is excellent news regarding autoimmune causes. Given the restrictive pattern on your lung function tests and the interstitial infiltrates seen on the X-ray, have you noticed any dry, scratchy cough that worsens at night, or any history of exposure to dust, mold, or bird droppings? REQUEST TEST: Serum Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme (ACE) and Soluble Fas Ligand.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the autoimmune and sarcoidosis markers are normal, have you noticed any unexplained weight loss, night sweats, or fatigue recently? REQUEST TEST: Soluble Fas Ligand (confirmatory) and High-Resolution CT of the Chest.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Soluble Fas Ligand: Normal; High-Resolution CT of the Chest: Not performed in current dataset.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF). The combination of a restrictive lung pattern, bilateral interstitial infiltrates on X-ray, and the absence of autoimmune, sarcoidosis, or infectious markers strongly supports this diagnosis.
